subject: Request: Third-Party Controls & Subprocessor Evidence Handbook
messages:
From: Jane Sato <jane.sato@novomed.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Patel <amit.patel@riskpartners.io>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Third-party evidence: packaged controls mapping request

Hi Vanessa,

As part of NovoMed's annual SIG review we need a compact, machine-readable package that maps Redwood's control families to the actual artifacts we can reference (e.g., SOC 2 report section, repository path, Drive file, and the owning person). Our security team asked for: a single CSV that lists each control, the control description, status (implemented/in-progress), primary owner, and link to evidence.

The request is a bit time-boxed — target delivery is end of week (EOW). If you have an existing "controls handbook" or a subprocessor mapping that we can validate, that would be ideal. If not, a stub with the top 25 controls and owners is fine; we can iterate.

Attachments: none from our side.

Thanks,
Jane Sato
Head of Vendor Security, NovoMed
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Jane Sato <jane.sato@novomed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Third-party evidence: packaged controls mapping request

Jane — thanks for the clear ask.

Quick status: we have an internal subprocessor snapshot and a controls inventory but they are not yet consolidated in the exact CSV format you described. I pulled the current subprocessor snapshot and attached a CSV export (redwood_subproc_snapshot_20260411.csv) showing vendor names, data scope, and last attestation dates.

Plan proposition:
- Marissa will own the controls-to-evidence mapping doc and populate the first pass for the top availability/security controls.
- Ben will pull the SOC 2 references and point to the responsible repos/Drive locations.
- I'll assemble everything into the requested CSV template and deliver a package by EOW for your review.

Attached: redwood_subproc_snapshot_20260411.csv; I also attached a blank controls_handbook_template_v1.docx (internal) that mirrors the fields you requested.

Do you have a preferred naming convention for links (we can include Drive URLs or internal artifact ids)?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_subproc_snapshot_20260411.csv (CSV), controls_handbook_template_v1.docx (DOCX)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Sato <jane.sato@novomed.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Third-party evidence: packaged controls mapping request

Looping in the plan so we're aligned. Vanessa — I'll scaffold the controls handbook in Drive and tag each control with: control_id, control_family, short_desc, status, owner, evidence_link, last_review. Ben — can you add the SOC 2 section references (e.g., CC1.1, CC3.2) to the evidence_link field where applicable?

I've started a folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cControlsHandbook (internal). Please add any checked-in artifacts rather than copying large binaries. For artifacts that are not shareable (e.g., certain internal runbooks), add an internal reference and mark them as "available on request". 

Priority notes: NovoMed is particularly focused on data residency and key management for subprocessors that handle PII. Please flag any vendor with cross-region processing so we can call that out.

I'll try to get the first 30 controls populated by EOD tomorrow.

—Marissa
Director, Security Programs, Redwood Inference
Attachment: controls_handbook_template_v1.docx (updated)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Sato <jane.sato@novomed.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Third-party evidence: packaged controls mapping request

Marissa — thanks, I'm on it. Quick clarification: our biometric provider (BioKey Inc.) was ingested as a subprocessor for fraud-detection telemetry in 2025 — is that in scope for NovoMed's SIG? They only signed a limited processing addendum but they do handle hashed device identifiers and behavioral signals; some teams consider that moderately sensitive.

If BioKey is in scope we should:
- Mark them as "in-scope: yes" in the CSV and include the PIA link and DPA clause reference.
- Confirm KMS usage — we don't send raw keys, but we need to confirm where the telemetry is stored and if keys are customer-specific.

I'll start adding SOC references and the PIA links to the Drive doc. Vanessa — I'll drop comments inline where I need input from product/security.

Ben Carter
Vendor Risk Manager, Redwood Inference
